# Setup

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Configure the report and reproducible random seed.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
set.seed(415)
```

```{r packages}
# Load packages required for statistical comparisons.
required_packages <- c("dplyr", "tidyr", "ggplot2", "knitr")
missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop("Install these packages first: ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "))
}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
```

# Load Data

```{r load_data}
# Find the project root whether knitting from code/ or the project root.
project_root <- if (file.exists("data/processed/pre_covid_clean.csv")) {
  "."
} else if (file.exists("../data/processed/pre_covid_clean.csv")) {
  ".."
} else {
  stop("Cannot locate data/processed/pre_covid_clean.csv. Open the project .Rproj first.")
}

# Read the two processed datasets without modifying the originals.
pre_path <- file.path(project_root, "data", "processed", "pre_covid_clean.csv")
post_path <- file.path(project_root, "data", "processed", "post_covid_clean.csv")

if (!file.exists(post_path)) {
  stop("Missing processed post-COVID dataset: ", post_path)
}

pre_covid <- read.csv(pre_path, check.names = FALSE)
post_covid <- read.csv(post_path, check.names = FALSE)

# Check the shared variables needed for comparisons.
required_columns <- c("PHQ", "GAD", "gender", "field", "race.2",
                      "yr_sch.2", "fincur.2", "age")

for (dataset_name in c("pre_covid", "post_covid")) {
  missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, names(get(dataset_name)))
  if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
    stop(dataset_name, " is missing: ", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", "))
  }
}

# Confirm sample sizes.
data.frame(
  Dataset = c("Pre-COVID (2017–2018)", "Post-COVID (2022–2023)"),
  N = c(nrow(pre_covid), nrow(post_covid))
) |> knitr::kable()
```

# Clean Pre-COVID and Post-COVID Data

```{r analysis_01}
# Standardize survey periods and demographic categories across datasets.
# Convert outcomes and numeric predictors to numeric values, then combine the samples.
pre_covid$Period <- "2017-2018 Pre-COVID"
post_covid$Period <- "2022-2023 Post-COVID"

post_covid$field <- as.character(post_covid$field)
pre_covid$field <- as.character(pre_covid$field)

post_covid$field[post_covid$field == "NotSTEM"] <- "Non-STEM"
pre_covid$field[pre_covid$field == "NotSTEM"] <- "Non-STEM"

pre_covid$gender <- factor(
  pre_covid$gender,
  levels = c("Men", "Women")
)

post_covid$gender <- factor(
  post_covid$gender,
  levels = c("Men", "Women")
)

pre_covid$field <- factor(
  pre_covid$field,
  levels = c("Non-STEM", "STEM")
)

post_covid$field <- factor(
  post_covid$field,
  levels = c("Non-STEM", "STEM")
)

race_levels <- c(
  "White",
  "Asian",
  "Black",
  "Hispanic",
  "Middle Eastern"
)

pre_covid$race.2 <- factor(
  pre_covid$race.2,
  levels = race_levels
)

post_covid$race.2 <- factor(
  post_covid$race.2,
  levels = race_levels
)

year_levels <- c(
  "firstyear",
  "secondyear",
  "thirdyear",
  "fourthyear+"
)

pre_covid$yr_sch.2 <- factor(
  pre_covid$yr_sch.2,
  levels = year_levels
)

post_covid$yr_sch.2 <- factor(
  post_covid$yr_sch.2,
  levels = year_levels
)

pre_covid$PHQ <- as.numeric(pre_covid$PHQ)
pre_covid$GAD <- as.numeric(pre_covid$GAD)
pre_covid$fincur.2 <- as.numeric(pre_covid$fincur.2)
pre_covid$age <- as.numeric(pre_covid$age)

post_covid$PHQ <- as.numeric(post_covid$PHQ)
post_covid$GAD <- as.numeric(post_covid$GAD)
post_covid$fincur.2 <- as.numeric(post_covid$fincur.2)
post_covid$age <- as.numeric(post_covid$age)

combined <- bind_rows(
  pre_covid,
  post_covid
)

combined$Period <- factor(
  combined$Period,
  levels = c(
    "2017-2018 Pre-COVID",
    "2022-2023 Post-COVID"
  )
)
```

# Pre-COVID vs Post-COVID Hypothesis Tests

## Depression

```{r analysis_02}
# Use a two-sample t-test to compare average depression (PHQ) scores
# between the pre-COVID and post-COVID survey periods.
phq_test <- t.test(
  PHQ ~ Period,
  data = combined
)

phq_test
```

*Interpretation note:* Use the numerical output above when reporting the direction, magnitude, and significance of this comparison.

## Anxiety

```{r analysis_03}
# Use a two-sample t-test to compare average anxiety (GAD) scores
# between the pre-COVID and post-COVID survey periods.
gad_test <- t.test(
  GAD ~ Period,
  data = combined
)

gad_test
```

*Interpretation note:* Use the numerical output above when reporting the direction, magnitude, and significance of this comparison.

# Student Characteristic Differences

## Age

```{r analysis_04}
# Test whether the average student age differs between survey periods.
age_test <- t.test(
  age ~ Period,
  data = combined
)

age_test
```

*Interpretation note:* Use the numerical output above when reporting the direction, magnitude, and significance of this comparison.

## Financial Stress

```{r analysis_05}
# Compare average current financial stress scores across survey periods.
financial_test <- t.test(
  fincur.2 ~ Period,
  data = combined
)

financial_test
```

*Interpretation note:* Use the numerical output above when reporting the direction, magnitude, and significance of this comparison.

## Gender

```{r analysis_06}
# Create a period-by-gender frequency table and use a chi-square test
# to examine whether the gender distribution differs across periods.
gender_table <- table(
  combined$Period,
  combined$gender
)

gender_table

gender_test <- chisq.test(
  gender_table
)

gender_test
```

*Interpretation note:* Use the numerical output above when reporting the direction, magnitude, and significance of this comparison.

## STEM Status

```{r analysis_07}
# Compare the proportion of STEM and non-STEM students across periods
# using a contingency table and chi-square test.
stem_table <- table(
  combined$Period,
  combined$field
)

stem_table

stem_test <- chisq.test(
  stem_table
)

stem_test
```

*Interpretation note:* Use the numerical output above when reporting the direction, magnitude, and significance of this comparison.

```{r analysis_08}
race_table
```

```{r analysis_09}

year_table

year_test
```

# Depression Changes by Gender

```{r analysis_10}
# Compare pre- and post-COVID depression scores separately for men
# and women using two-sample t-tests within each gender group.
men_phq <- t.test(
  PHQ ~ Period,
  data = combined %>%
    filter(gender == "Men")
)

women_phq <- t.test(
  PHQ ~ Period,
  data = combined %>%
    filter(gender == "Women")
)

men_phq
women_phq
```

*Interpretation note:* Use the numerical output above when reporting the direction, magnitude, and significance of this comparison.

# Did Relationships Change After COVID?

## Depression and Gender

```{r analysis_14}
# Fit a period-by-gender interaction model for depression to assess
# whether the gender difference in PHQ scores varies by survey period.
phq_gender_interaction <- lm(
  PHQ ~ Period * gender,
  data = combined
)

summary(phq_gender_interaction)
```

*Interpretation note:* Use the numerical output above when reporting the direction, magnitude, and significance of this comparison.


# Adjusted Pre/Post Models

## Adjusted Depression Model

```{r analysis_18}
# Estimate the difference in depression scores between survey periods
# while adjusting for gender, STEM status, race, year, financial stress, and age.
adjusted_phq <- lm(
  PHQ ~ Period +
    gender +
    field +
    race.2 +
    yr_sch.2 +
    fincur.2 +
    age,
  data = combined
)

summary(adjusted_phq)
```

*Interpretation note:* Use the numerical output above when reporting the direction, magnitude, and significance of this comparison.

## Adjusted Anxiety Model

```{r analysis_19}
# Estimate the difference in anxiety scores between survey periods
# while adjusting for gender, STEM status, race, year, financial stress, and age.
adjusted_gad <- lm(
  GAD ~ Period +
    gender +
    field +
    race.2 +
    yr_sch.2 +
    fincur.2 +
    age,
  data = combined
)

summary(adjusted_gad)
```

*Interpretation note:* Use the numerical output above when reporting the direction, magnitude, and significance of this comparison.


# Results Tables

```{r comparison_table}
# Summarize the raw PHQ and GAD differences by period.
period_summary <- combined %>%
  group_by(Period) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    PHQ_N = sum(!is.na(PHQ)),
    PHQ_Mean = mean(PHQ, na.rm = TRUE),
    PHQ_SD = sd(PHQ, na.rm = TRUE),
    GAD_N = sum(!is.na(GAD)),
    GAD_Mean = mean(GAD, na.rm = TRUE),
    GAD_SD = sd(GAD, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(period_summary, digits = 3,
             caption = "Depression and anxiety by survey period")
```

```{r regression_tables}
# Present adjusted regression coefficients in compact tables.
regression_table <- function(model, outcome) {
  coef_table <- as.data.frame(summary(model)$coefficients)
  coef_table$Term <- rownames(coef_table)
  rownames(coef_table) <- NULL
  names(coef_table)[1:4] <- c("Estimate", "Std_Error", "T_Value", "P_Value")
  coef_table$Outcome <- outcome
  coef_table[, c("Outcome", "Term", "Estimate", "Std_Error", "T_Value", "P_Value")]
}

adjusted_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  regression_table(adjusted_phq, "PHQ"),
  regression_table(adjusted_gad, "GAD")
)

knitr::kable(adjusted_results, digits = 4,
             caption = "Adjusted PHQ and GAD regression coefficients")
```

```{r model_diagnostics}
# Check residual patterns for the two adjusted models.
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(adjusted_phq, which = 1, main = "PHQ residuals")
plot(adjusted_gad, which = 1, main = "GAD residuals")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
